question.problem: Find the numbers $c$ such that the average value of $f(x)=9{x}^{2}+6x-18$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $0.$
question.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 0 & =\frac{1}{c-0}{\int }_{0}^{c}(9{x}^{2}+6x-18)\,\text{d}x \\ 0 & ={\frac{1}{c}(3{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}-18x)|}_{0}^{c} \\ 0 & =\frac{1}{c}[(3{c}^{3}+3{c}^{2}-18c)-0] \\ 0 & =3{c}^{2}+3c-18 \\ 0 & =(c+3)(3c-6) \\ c & =-3,\,2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $c>0,$ we conclude that $c=2$ only.
